bihar_raw_news.title: RVNL Wins ₹903 Cr Order from SJVN for Buxar Thermal Siding - PSU Connect
bihar_raw_news.content: New Delhi: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited has secured a major infrastructure order linked to one of SJVN’s key thermal projects. The company has received a Letter of Award from SJVN Thermal Private Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary of SJVN Limited) for the construction of a permanent railway siding along with an aerial track connection from the plant boundary to Chausa and Pawani Kamarpur at Buxar in Bihar. The work forms Phase-III of the infrastructure support for the 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project (BTPP). Follow PSU Connect: WhatsApp Order details • Value: ₹903.01 crore (including GST) • Scope: Permanent siding + aerial track connection • Location: Buxar, Bihar • Completion period: 36 months • Nature: Domestic order in the normal course of business RVNL confirmed that the promoter or promoter group has no interest in the awarding entity and that the transaction does not fall under related-party transactions. The disclosure was made to the stock exchanges under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. Advertisement AD Follow PSU Connect: LinkedIn

national_raw_news.title: 26 mins ago | National 30 Teachers day: President Droupadi Murmu to confer National Awards on school teachers in New Delhi ...
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has called upon teachers and educators to continually update their knowledge, embrace technology, and adopt innovative teaching methods. In her message on the occasion of Teachers’ Day today, the President said teachers and educators play a vital role in nurturing talent and strengthening character through their guidance and mentorship. She said, dedicated and caring teachers can recognise the unique potential of students, inspire them, and encourage them to strive for excellence. President Murmu also urged teachers to promote independent thinking and cultivate a spirit of enquiry among students. Expressing gratitude to all dedicated teachers for their contributions, the President wished them continued success in nurturing enlightened generations who will take the nation to greater heights. President Murmu also paid tribute to former President Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. She described him as an extraordinary teacher. Teachers’ Day is observed every year on 5th of September to mark the birth anniversary of former President Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, who was a renowned educationist, author, and philosopher. The day honours the vital role of teachers and educators in nation-building. Teachers transform the lives of students, shape generations, and strengthen the foundations of society. On the occasion, President Droupadi Murmu will confer the National Teachers’ Awards on 48 school teachers in New Delhi this morning. The 48 selected teachers are from 27 States, seven Union Territories, and six Central Government organisations. The President will also present National Awards to 21 teachers and faculty members from higher education institutions and polytechnics. Twelve teachers and faculty members are from Central Higher Education Institutions, five from state universities, including three government and two private colleges, and four from polytechnics, including two government and two private polytechnics. Short documentaries showcasing the exemplary work of each awardee will also be screened at the event.

national_raw_news.title: 34 mins ago | National 25 EAM S Jaishankar says India in continuous touch with Ukraine & Russia to help end the conflict
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said India is in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia. He said New Delhi is exploring ideas and suggestions that could help mitigate or end the conflict. Dr Jaishankar made the remarks while addressing a joint press conference with Poland’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski following their talks in Warsaw yesterday. The External Affairs Minister reiterated that India believes that endless war must give way to an end to war. He said wars have no winners and only lead to more deaths, destruction and global costs. He added that efforts should focus on promoting dialogue and diplomacy. He said India is committed to doing whatever it can to help bring the conflict to an end. Dr Jaishankar reached Poland after visiting Ukraine, where he held talks with top Ukrainian leadership on Thursday. During the media briefing, the External Affairs Minister said he discussed with his Polish counterpart the complex global challenges, including supply chain resilience and food, fuel and fertiliser security. Both sides also reviewed the progress of the Joint Action Plan 2024-28, which focuses on trade and investment, defence, culture and multilateral cooperation. Later, Dr Jaishankar also called on Polish President Karol Nawrocki and discussed the bilateral Strategic Partnership and exchanged views on the Ukraine conflict and the West Asia situation. In Kyiv, Dr Jaishankar said that India is ready to extend any help in any manner to end the Ukraine-Russia war. He had also met President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and his Ukrainian counterpart Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv on Thursday. After talks with the External Affairs Minister, President Zelenskyy said that he was grateful to India for its commitment to ending the war.

national_raw_news.title: 37 mins ago | International 33 UN votes to adopt new world map reflecting accurate size of Africa
national_raw_news.content: The UN General Assembly has voted to replace the traditional world map with one that more accurately reflects the size of Africa. The “Correct the Map” resolution, sponsored by Togo and backed by African Union (AU) members, passed with the support of 164 nations, including France and the UK. The United States was the only nation to vote against it while six countries abstained. The UN vote is non-binding, but it will encourage governments and institutions to stop using the traditional Mercator map. The Mercator map, which has been in common use since the 16th Century, has come in for criticism as it shows Africa as similar in size to Greenland, even though it is 14 times larger. Critics say this leads to the development needs and potential for countries near the equator to be minimised. The Mercator map was designed in 1569 by the Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator to help European explorers navigate across the world. The map makes countries near the poles appear much larger than they really are. The distortion of his map is a result of the fact that it is impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart. In an effort to correct this, a team of cartographers in 2018 created an equal area map they called the Equal Earth projection which shows the relative sizes of continents more accurately. In February, the African Union’s 54 member states adopted it, and said it more accurately represents the sizes of all continents, particularly Africa. Ahead of the voting, Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey talking to the media, said a fair world begins with a fair map. At a UN briefing, Mr Dussey said, a map is never neutral. It shapes perceptions and influences how the place of peoples and continents in the world is understood. France has also backed the change and said it plans to stop using the Mercator map. However, the United States criticised the UN vote, arguing that the General Assembly should focus on more serious global issues. Campaigners say maps are more than just guides for travellers, they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically.
